full_judgment:
Md Abu Zafor Siddique J: This criminal appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 31-5-2022 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.30285 of 2022 disposing of. the application filed by respondent No.2 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure without issuing any Rule with direction upon the learned Joint Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Meherpur to take step to get the signature of respondent No.2 contained in the alleged Cheque examined by a hand-writing expert. 

 2. The facts of the case, in short, are that on 19-8-2019 the appellant Md Amam Hossain Milu as complainant filed a CR Case bearing No.126 of 2019 (Mujibnagar) before the learned Senior Judicial Magistrate, 1st Court, Meherpur under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (as amended in 2006) against respondent No.2 alleging, inter alia, that respondent No.2 on 27-4-2019 for payment of money due to the complainant gave a cheque bearing No.CA-503171089 dated 27-4-2019 for an amount of Taka 1,02,78,600 (one crore two lac seventy eight thousand and six hundred) from his account of Sonali Bank Ltd., Daulatpur College Road Branch, Khulna to the appellant and thereafter on 12-6-2019 the appellant placed the same to the Sonali Bank Ltd., Court Building Branch, Meherpur for encashment and on 23-6-2019 the same was dishonoured due to insufficient fund and on the same date the Manager of the said Bank issued a certificate regarding the same and lastly on 30-6-2019 the appellant sent a legal notice and after receiving that respondent No.2 did not take any initiative regarding the same and that was the reason for filing the case. 

 3. Thereafter, the learned Magistrate took cognizance and summoned respondent No.2 and on 15-10-2019 he voluntarily surrendered before the learned Magistrate and obtained bail in connection with the case and after complying with all the formalities the learned Magistrate transferred the case to the Court of learned Sessions Judge, Meherpur for trial and it was renumbered as Sessions Case No.260 of 2019 and on 24-11-2019 the learned Sessions Judge, Meherpur framed charge under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 against respondent No.2 in his presence. 

 4. Then, the case was sent to the Court of learned Joint Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Meherpur for trial and disposal. On 13-9-2021 the learned trial Court below recorded the deposition of PW Nos.1 and 2 in connection with the case. On the same date respondent No.2 made an application before the learned Trial Court for taking hand writing expert's opinion after examining the signature allegedly to have been put in the said cheque and subsequently on 25-10-2021 the learned trial Court rejected his prayer and also fixed the next date for examining defence witness on 25-11-2021. 

 6. Upon hearing the parties and considering the evidence and materials on record the learned Sessions Judge, Meherpur by his judgment and order dated 24-3-2022 dismissed the application. Being aggrieved, respondent No.2 preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.30285 of 2022 before the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure which was disposed of without issuing any Rule by directing the learned Joint Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Meherpur to take step to get the signature of respondent No.2 contained in the cheque examined by a hand writing expert. Hence, the instant criminal appeal is filed before this Division by the complainant. 

 7. Mr AM Mahbub Uddin, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant referring to the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division submits that the High Court Division without issuing any Rule has given full relief to respondent No.2 herein by disposing of the application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and, as such, violated the settled principle of natural justice which is not permissible in law. He further submits that the High Court Division has failed to appreciate that respondent No.2 from the inception is trying to delay the trial by filing an application under section 526B of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the learned Sessions Judge, Meherpur. The appellant as had already been examined as PW I and the Manager of the Sonali Bank Ltd, Meherpur Court building Branch was examined as PW2 on 13-9-2021 and the said witnesses were cross-examined by the defence. Subsequently, on 12-5-2022 respondent No.2 adduced two witnesses as DW 1, himself, and DW2, the Manager of the Sonali Bank Ltd, Daulatpur College Road Branch, Khulna who had admitted in his deposition that the cheque was dishonoured due to insufficient fund and respondent No.2 had drawn the cheque in the name of the appellant. Then after completion of argument hearing the trial Court fixed the date for judgment on 6-6-2022. The application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure was filed with the object to delay the delivery of judgment. The learned Senior Advocate also submits that the High Court Division erred in law in disposing the application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure without giving any opportunity for hearing to the opposite party (complainant) inasmuch as the said order which is tantamount to full and complete relief prayed for in the memo of criminal miscellaneous case and, as such, the same is liable to be set-aside. 

 8. Mr Faysal Hasan Arif, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent No.2 submits that the signature contained in the cheque in question is not his signature and he never issued any such cheque to the appellant. He also submits that in a case under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act, proof of signature of the accused on the cheque is very important for determination of guilt or innocence of the accused and, as such, respondent No.2 herein filed an application for examination of the signature on the cheque by a hand writing expert which the High Court Division has rightly appreciated and passed the impugned judgment. Accordingly the learned Advocate submits that the impugned judgment being fully in consonance with law the same does not call for any interference in this appeal. Hence the appeal should be dismissed. 

 11. Let us first answer to the question as to whether the High Court Division exercising power under section 561A can grant full relief to the applicant without issuing rule and without affording opportunity for hearing to the other party. In this respect this Division in the case of Gulf Air Company (GSC) and another vs Travel Trade Ltd. and others reported in 65 DLR (AD) 141 held as follows: 

 12. In the said decision this Division did not endorse such kind of action. This Division in the said case has discouraged the High Court Division from giving full relief without issuing Rule and without enabling the other side to give answer on the allegation by way of affidavit. The High Court Division by the impugned judgment disposed of the application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and directed the learned Joint Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Meherpur to take step to get the signature contained in the cheque examined by a hand writing expert. But before issuing such direction the High Court Division ought to have issued rule as it was held by this Division earlier in the aforementioned case. Accordingly, we are unable to differ from the view expressed in the above judgment. 

 13. So far the question raised by the appellant that respondent No.2 is trying to make delay in disposal of the proceeding by filing the application for getting his signature examined by hand writing expert when admittedly the cheque in question was dishonoured on presentation in the Bank for encashment due to insufficient fund. The appellant as complainant filed CR case No.126 of 2019 under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act against respondent No.2. During the trial 2(two) PWs were examined and cross-examined and 2(two) DWs were examined and cross-examined. It appears that in cross-examination by the defence specific suggestion was given to PW1 (appellant-complainant) that the signature contained in the cheque in question was not the signature of the accused. DW1 in his cross-examination stated that he did not give any such cheque and pad to the complainant and also denied the receiving of any legal notice. DW2 was the Principal Officer of the Bank who in his cross-examination stated that the cheque was presented to the Bank but due to insufficiency of fund it was dishonoured. 

 14. It appears that on the day of examination of PWs respondent No.2 filed an application before the trial Court for getting the signature contained in the impugned cheque examined by hand writing expert alleging that he did not sign the impugned cheque or give any acknowledgment in favour of the complainant and, as such, he prayed for examination of the signature on the cheque in question and the acknowledgement given in pad with his specimen signature kept in the Bank by hand writing expert. But, the trial Court rejected the application vide order dated 25-10-2021. Challenging the said rejection order respondent No.2 filed Criminal Revision No.30 of 2021 before the learned Sessions Judge, Meherpur and the learned Sessions Judge, Meherpur vide judgment and order dated 24-3-2022 rejected his prayer. Hence, respondent No.2 moved the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The High Court Division as we have already noticed that without issuing any rule directed the trial Court to get the disputed signature in the cheque examined along with the specimen signature kept in the Bank by hand writing expert as prayed for by respondent No.2. It is fact that whether the drawer of the cheque is guilty or innocent depends upon the proof of signature of the accused on the cheque in question. In that context, while holding a trial dispensation of justice demands consideration of the prayer as sought for by respondent No.2 in this case. There is no doubt that Court is the expert of all experts. Even though since respondent No.2 prayed with a specific prayer for getting the signature on the cheque and the acknowledgement in the pad with his specimen signature kept in the Bank examined by hand writing expert, it would be wise, safe and sound to leave the matter of such examination to the expert and ask for report by scientific process or method as has been developed much better than before. 

 15. In the facts and circumstances as stated above and since the examination of the witnesses has been completed, we are of the view that if the trial Court finds it necessary for ensuring the ends of justice to seek expert opinion regarding the signature contained in the impugned cheque for proper and effective disposal of the case then it shall be at liberty to ask for an expert opinion.
